# Where does retrieval coverage come from? User representations, positive examples, and negative difficulty

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/retrieval-matching.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-26 · 43 topic entries / 11 representative comparisons

Candidate generation determines what downstream ranking can see. YouTube DNN uses one user vector for nearest-neighbor retrieval; Airbnb EBR ties supervision to the search–browse–booking journey; MIMA allocates multiple positives from a request to complementary interests; MDCNS changes negative difficulty and provides multi-view supervision. These alter representations, labels, interest specialization, and gradients, respectively. More retrieved candidates are not a common explanation.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Locate the bottleneck: coverage, supervision, or interest collapse

YouTube DNN compresses history into one user vector. Airbnb EBR keeps a similar retrieval interface but reorganizes journey supervision. A similar dual-encoder shape does not make their training problems equivalent. MIMA's defining change is one-to-one assignment of same-request positives, not merely emitting more vectors; otherwise interests may converge on one positive. Fix the final return budget to separate better representations from retrieving more items.

Sources: [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md) · [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md)

### Hard negatives and multiple positives have different roles

MDCNS finds unobserved candidates models find difficult and disagree on, giving Self full-pool teacher supervision. MIMA learns interest specialization from real positive sets. Labeling all unclicked items as negatives or treating adjacent behaviors as complementary same-request positives changes the meaning of supervision. Airbnb EBR's journey reminds us to record behavioral stages and exposure before interpreting a lower loss.

Sources: [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md)

### A cluster constrains candidates instead of assigning a unique semantic path

WeSearch retains atomic documents inside a cluster union and separates coarse ranking from feature-aware ranking. MIMA instead lets multiple user interests propose candidates. Both require a fixed final deduplicated budget when comparing coverage; collecting more candidates does not establish better representations. The ADC identity verifies computation for one quantized representation, and fixed-artifact mounting does not replace training or coordinated model/index refresh.

Sources: [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md)

### Reusing logs is not a new matching representation

WeSearch narrows the retrieval space with clusters, then scores by OPQ and features. URED relies on existing scores and accumulates unshown items into another channel. Keep recall and display quotas fixed and audit deduplication, freshness and exposure.

Sources: [From Waste to Discovery: Recycling High-Scored Unexposed Candidates in Taobao Feed Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.05997-ured/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### yuanbao-rubric: distinguish mechanism from capability

Sections2.1 and Eqs4–6 are implemented. Positive criteria can be covered collectively and any document can trigger a deduction. Focal pairwise ranking uses a label-gap minus score-gap hinge, not ordinary CE. Each selection branch has its own mean; poor-rollout weights multiply the same best-trajectory token NLL. Padding, empty branches and tied zero updates are preserved. Reference KL is an explicit caller input, not an invented estimator. WeSearch narrows candidates using clusters and atomic document matching; Yuanbao aligns upstream labels with final subset rewards. They are not the same SID/retrieval architecture, and neither local ADC nor the dual-branch loss replaces end-to-end search validation.

Sources: [From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.22503-yuanbao-rubric/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### intentflow: distinguish mechanism from capability

Eqs16,18–21 and24 are implemented: one query gate mixes two shared-bottleneck branches (paper ranks8/64), retaining a frozen base projection. Both distillation directions share valid candidate sets and detach the teacher. CSLS subtracts only offline document density relative to a training-query bank. Zero-initialized up projections are a local stability convention, not an initialization specified by the paper or a complete model recipe. WeSearch constrains candidates by clusters and atomic matching; IntentFlow defines evidence required by the request and adapts query encoding to a fixed document space. Candidate organization and intent-supervised representations differ, and component gradients prove neither online lift.

Sources: [IntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.20448-intentflow/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation

YouTube DNN transforms aggregated watch history/context through a nonlinear user tower and trains next-watch classification. LSER separately encodes session/history and may add LLM semantic auxiliaries with nearline refresh. Both query an offline item index using user vectors; the difference is representation and freshness, not replacing ANN with token-by-token LLM generation. The paper's online control is rules, not YouTube DNN; local interfaces do not rank their quality. Session windows use logged session IDs; history ends at session start, and every event is strictly before the label/request cutoff. Eligibility, ID mapping, lookback and sessionization are external contracts, not invented receipt schemas. The paper prescribes no universal TTL. Choosing by(as_of,written_at) against out-of-order completion is a local interface safeguard.

Sources: [From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.26096-lser-serving/README-en.md) · [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md)

### Shared Yuanbao Search context does not make document grades and set utility identical

LARF Eqs.3–5 exclude gold ties, give half credit to predicted ties and scale ordered concordance by group size. Yuanbao Rubric allows joint positive coverage and negative triggers from any document. LARF Eqs.8–10 choose the strongest among all non-gold digit classes, not only adjacent grades; Eq.12 retains generation in training and deletes it only in serving. Gold-conditioned CoT is training-target construction, not gold visibility for an evaluated agent. Both real production baselines matter, but HSR/LSR differ from GSB, and LARF8B offline50.98 is not the deployed1.7B student's result.

Sources: [LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.32125-larf/README-en.md) · [From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.22503-yuanbao-rubric/README-en.md)

### Can QT reward be replaced by LARF's ordinal distance?

LARF models five ordinal relevance attributes of one document with PNR, rule feedback and terminal-digit margins. OneQuery instead supervises four heterogeneous structured fields of one query. Its QT reward requires whole-set exact matching, not LARF's graded distance or inter-document ordering. LARF's training generation/serving classification split also differs from OneQuery's head cache/tail distillation. Their production metrics are not directly comparable.

Sources: [OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.33653-onequery/README-en.md) · [LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.32125-larf/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If recall rises after MIMA returns multiple interests, how can we distinguish complementarity from a larger candidate budget? {#cross-more-interests-not-more-budget}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Fix total K after merging and deduplicating channels, then compare with single-vector retrieval. Check whether positive assignments and hits complement each other. The mechanism is MIMA's one-to-one supervision and activation calibration; YouTube DNN gives a single-vector starting point. Giving each interest an extra K makes a coverage gain impossible to attribute to interest modeling alone.

    **Illustrative example:** If running and photography each return 50 items, compare the merged 100-item budget to one channel with 100, not 50.

    Sources: [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md)

### Why do Airbnb EBR and MDCNS emphasize negatives without simply taking the highest-scoring unclicked item as the best negative? {#cross-hard-negative-is-not-ground-truth}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Airbnb interprets hard negatives in their journey and behavioral stage. MDCNS uses disagreement across views rather than only Self's preferences. A non-click can reflect underexposure, substitution, or a missing label. A high score means the current model sees similarity, not that the item is certainly irrelevant. Control false negatives, diversity, and sampling budget.

    **Illustrative example:** A user booked one property, but two other suitable properties were sold out. Treating them as definitely irrelevant mistakes inventory outcomes for semantic preferences.

    Sources: [Applying Embedding-Based Retrieval to Airbnb Search](../../../../reproductions/2601.06873-airbnb-ebr/README-en.md) · [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md)

### Why can't a stronger ranker recover an interest missed by retrieval, and where can a new training objective help? {#cross-recall-versus-ranking-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The ranker only sorts existing candidates. YouTube DNN separates the stages; MIMA changes which interests nominate candidates using multi-positive assignments; MDCNS changes the negative gradients received by retrieval representations. Check coverage, fixed-K quality, and downstream ranking separately instead of diagnosing the bottleneck from clicks alone.

    **Illustrative example:** If all 100 candidates are running shoes, a ranker cannot show a camera. Multi-interest retrieval must nominate the camera before ranking can compare its value with the shoes.

    Sources: [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md) · [MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment](../../../../reproductions/2609.12842-mima/README-en.md) · [Divergence Meets Consensus: A Multi-Source Negative Sampling Framework for Sequential Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2605.19651-mdcns/README-en.md)

### Can URED recover a document that has never entered a historical ranking pool? {#cross-candidate-pool-history-versus-clusters}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It consumes historical ranker outputs. A retrieval index such as WeSearch's can surface a first candidate in an available snapshot; the channels are not substitutes.

    **Illustrative example:** Example: A new item may enter a refreshed index, but cannot appear in the URED log pool before any request scores it.

    Sources: [From Waste to Discovery: Recycling High-Scored Unexposed Candidates in Taobao Feed Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.05997-ured/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### Does Yuanbao change the same layer as WeSearch? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-yuanbao-rubric}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It aligns utility supervision and subset selection; WeSearch primarily changes atomic matching within cluster-constrained candidates.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: correct ADC distances do not prove a final evidence set is nonredundant, complete or current.

    Sources: [From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.22503-yuanbao-rubric/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### How does it differ from WeSearch cluster constraints? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-intentflow}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Fixed-index adaptation changes how a query maps into existing document space; cluster constraints organize candidates. They can combine but are not substitutes.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: changing query residuals with bitwise-unchanged documents proves only the fixed-index interface.

    Sources: [IntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.20448-intentflow/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

### What does LSER add beyond YouTube DNN rather than generating recommendations with an LLM? {#cross-nov20-lser-serving}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** YouTube DNN aggregates history/context into a user tower. LSER separates short/long sequence encoders and adds optional LLM features plus asynchronous freshness. Both can query an offline item index; the LLM does not generate item IDs token by token.

    **Illustrative example:** With LLM vectors disabled, LSER remains learned two-tower retrieval; this is the version used in its online A/B.

    Sources: [From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.26096-lser-serving/README-en.md) · [Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en.md)

### Does high PNR imply that an evidence set satisfies the query rubric? {#cross-nov25-larf-pnr}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. PNR checks whether predicted document grades reproduce gold order within a query. Rubric set utility concerns joint coverage and negative triggers. Correct order can still miss key facts or include a penalized document.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: two correctly ordered documents both omit date evidence; PNR can be high with an uncovered timeliness criterion. Adding a dated source can improve coverage without changing their pair order.

    Sources: [LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.32125-larf/README-en.md) · [From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.22503-yuanbao-rubric/README-en.md)

### Can QT reward be replaced by LARF's ordinal distance? {#cross-nov26-onequery}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** LARF models five ordinal relevance attributes of one document with PNR, rule feedback and terminal-digit margins. OneQuery instead supervises four heterogeneous structured fields of one query. Its QT reward requires whole-set exact matching, not LARF's graded distance or inter-document ordering. LARF's training generation/serving classification split also differs from OneQuery's head cache/tail distillation. Their production metrics are not directly comparable.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: if the reference contains brand and product, missing either gives zero QT reward, not0.5 for matching half or an ordinal-distance score.

    Sources: [OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.33653-onequery/README-en.md) · [LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.32125-larf/README-en.md)

Affected: [IntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.20448-intentflow/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · No rubric generator, DeepSeek judge, Qwen encoder or real search is run. Diagnostics check best-trajectory imitation gradients, absent poor-trajectory imitation gradients, detached rewards and zero padding gradients; these are not answer-accuracy scores. Full experiments are not reproduced due to high cost; no capability or Evolve-promotion claim.

Affected: [From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.22503-yuanbao-rubric/README-en.md) · [WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en.md)
